reading: Every object shifts one cell to the left (cells pushed past the left edge are lost), then all background cells become 5.
why: each output fg cell is the input fg cell one column to its right; every other cell is 5

reading: Horizontal coloured lines cross one vertical 8-line (crossing cell 1). Each other row takes the colour of its nearest horizontal line (rows equidistant to two different colours become all 1), the vertical line becomes 1 in those rows, and each horizontal line becomes 1 with 8 at the crossing.

slots.lines: full rows without background colour 7 (the horizontal lines) and their colours
slots.band_colour: per row: colour of nearest line; tie between different colours -> 1 for whole row

why: every non-line row is uniform in its nearest line's colour except the column cell (1); tie rows all 1

reading: There are two shape kinds, each in its own colour; every copy of shape A is replaced by shape B (in B's colour) at the same box position, and vice versa.

slots.shape_a: the shape of one colour (all its objects identical)
slots.shape_b: the shape of the other colour
slots.placement: each object's bounding box top-left, replaced by the other shape and colour

why: each object box in the output holds the other colour's shape; the count and positions of objects unchanged

reading: Single coloured pixels on background 8 each move by an offset fixed by their colour: 7 up 2, 2 left 2, 9 down 2, 1 right 1.

slots.subject: markers (isolated single pixels)
slots.offset: a (dy,dx) per colour learned from training: 7->(-2,0), 2->(0,-2), 9->(2,0), 1->(0,1)

why: every pixel of colour c appears exactly at its input position plus offset(c); nothing else changes

reading: Each 1 sitting on top of a 5 stem drops straight down to the bottom row, replacing the 5 there; its old cell becomes background.
why: each colour-1 cell ends in the bottom row of its column; the stems stay

reading: Cells of colour 2 form loose clusters (2s at most one cell apart); inside each cluster's bounding box every non-2 cell becomes 4.

new_rows.name: box2
new_rows.datalog:
two(Y, X) :- cell(Y, X, 2).
near(A, B, C, D) :- two(A, B), two(C, D), DY = C - A, DX = D - B, DY >= -2, DY <= 2, DX >= -2, DX <= 2.
grp(A, B, C, D) :- near(A, B, C, D).
grp(A, B, E, F) :- grp(A, B, C, D), near(C, D, E, F).
gy0(A, B, min(C)) :- grp(A, B, C, D).
gy1(A, B, max(C)) :- grp(A, B, C, D).
gx0(A, B, min(D)) :- grp(A, B, C, D).
gx1(A, B, max(D)) :- grp(A, B, C, D).
box2(Y, X) :- gy0(A, B, Y0), gy1(A, B, Y1), gx0(A, B, X0), gx1(A, B, X1), px(Y, X, K), !two(Y, X), Y >= Y0, Y <= Y1, X >= X0, X <= X1.

why: every non-2 cell inside a 2-cluster's box is 4; all other cells unchanged

reading: Vertical bars of 8 and 2 stand on the bottom row in every other column; a new 5 bar is added two columns right of the last bar, bottom-aligned, with height = (number of 8 cells) - (number of 2 cells).

slots.height: count of colour 8 cells minus count of colour 2 cells

why: the only change is a colour-5 vertical run ending at the bottom row whose length is #8 - #2

reading: Around a two-colour pattern, every background cell that touches a shape cell only diagonally (no orthogonal shape neighbour) is painted with the pattern's inner (minority) colour.

new_rows.name: diag_only
new_rows.datalog:
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DY = 0.
orth(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), DX = 0.
diag(DY, DX) :- off(DY, DX), !orth(DY, DX).
bgc(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C).
otouch(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), orth(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).
dtouch(Y, X) :- bgc(Y, X), diag(DY, DX), Y2 = Y + DY, X2 = X + DX, cell(Y2, X2, C).
diag_only(Y, X) :- dtouch(Y, X), !otouch(Y, X).

slots.colour: the inner colour of the pattern (the one not on its outer edge): 2 in pair 1, 1 in pair 2; not one constant

why: every diag_only cell becomes the inner colour; nothing else changes

reading: A rectangle of colour A contains a centred block of colour B; a frame of colour B is added around the rectangle, its thickness equal to the inner block's width, but never more than the rectangle's smallest margin to the grid edge.
verb: add outer frame in inner colour

slots.subject: the outer rectangle (box of all fg)
slots.thickness: min(inner block width, smallest distance from rectangle to grid edge)
slots.placement: uniform ring on all four sides of the rectangle

why: output = input plus a ring of the inner colour of equal thickness on all sides of the rectangle
invariants: the original rectangle and its inner block

reading: Each 3-cell L-shaped 8 object fills its 2x2 box; the one missing corner cell becomes 1.

new_rows.name: box_holes
new_rows.datalog:
oy0(O, min(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
oy1(O, max(Y)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
ox0(O, min(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
ox1(O, max(X)) :- obj(O, Y, X).
box_holes(Y, X) :- px(Y, X, C), !cell(Y, X, C), oy0(O, A), oy1(O, B), ox0(O, D), ox1(O, E), Y >= A, Y <= B, X >= D, X <= E.

why: every background cell inside an object's bounding box becomes 1; nothing else changes
